why: Every figure has four white boxes sitting on the edges of the frame, and each white box has a dark box touching it. In figures 1, 2, 4 and 5 the white box is on the frame border and the dark box is pushed inward, towards the centre. In figure 3 it is the opposite: the dark boxes sit on the border and the white boxes are pushed inward. So figure 3 breaks the rule. Figure 1 looks different because its boxes are on all four sides, but the dark box is still inside, so it follows the rule.
trick: When boxes touch each other, ask which colour is on the border and which is inside. Check the same thing in every figure, and the one that reverses it is the odd one.
note: Rule is the position of dark vs white box (border or inside). Drawn from the PDF; the grey shading is simplified to flat black.
